key_insight: LSPO learns from the quality of reasoning transitions themselves by lifting each answer into a continuous state and optimizing energy descent through self-correction steps, rather than only scoring final outputs.
engineering_relevance: This enables single-pass generation to approach test-time reflection performance while cutting latency and token use, making it attractive for production LLM systems that need stronger reasoning efficiency.
method: Augment each textual answer with a learned continuous coordinate to form a lifted state.
Use an energy function plus shaped reward to favor low-energy transitions after accounting for edit and step costs.
Internalize selected low-energy answers into the base generator to reduce reliance on reflection at inference.
evidence_signal: On Qwen3.5-27B, LSPO achieved 71.8% aggregate accuracy across math, science, code, and logic benchmarks, nearly matching test-time reflection at 71.9% while using 28% lower latency and 25.8% fewer tokens.
watch_item: The approach adds learned transition geometry and cost shaping, so performance may depend on stable energy calibration and careful tuning of edit-step costs across backbones and tasks.
paper_title: Lifted State Policy Optimization: Internalizing Self-Correction through Transition Geometry
